question: What disciplines are integrated into nursing informatics according to the text?

options.A: Nursing science, computer science, and information science
options.C: Nursing practice, biology, and health administration
options.D: Information technology, statistics, and public health

explanation: Nursing informatics integrates nursing science, computer science, and information science to manage and communicate health data. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: Why is understanding basic software applications considered a core competency for modern nurses?

options.A: It replaces the need for direct patient bedside care
options.B: It streamlines clinical workflows, reduces errors, and improves patient outcomes
options.C: It is only required for administrative hospital directors
options.D: It eliminates all forms of verbal communication in the hospital

explanation: Software applications help streamline clinical workflows, reduce medical errors, and enhance overall patient care quality. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h1)

question: Which Microsoft Word feature is particularly useful for organizing patient assessment summaries or medication schedules?
explanation: Tables can be effectively used in documents to structure patient assessment summaries and medication administration schedules clearly. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h2)

question: Why are spell check and grammar features in word processors important in clinical documentation?

options.A: They completely automate the nursing diagnosis process
options.B: They minimize typos that could lead to clinical misunderstandings
options.C: They automatically submit reports to the Ministry of Health
options.D: They format the document into a spreadsheet format

question: What is a primary clinical or administrative use of Microsoft Excel in healthcare settings?

options.A: Drafting formal narrative patient stories and letters
options.B: Managing data, tracking statistics, and analyzing clinical trends
options.C: Designing complex vector graphics for hospital logos
options.D: Creating animated slide shows for patient orientation

explanation: Excel is used for data management, tracking statistics, calculating numbers, and analyzing clinical trends using spreadsheets and charts. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: How can a nurse manager utilize Excel charts when reviewing monthly malaria admission rates?

options.A: To translate clinical text into audio recordings
options.B: To create visual representations like bar charts aiding in resource allocation
options.C: To automatically order pharmaceutical supplies from vendors
options.D: To encrypt patient names for complete anonymity

explanation: Excel allows users to generate visual charts and graphs, such as bar charts, which help in analyzing peak periods and aiding resource allocation. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h3)

question: What is one of the main healthcare uses of Microsoft PowerPoint described in the text?

options.B: Designing engaging slide decks for patient education and staff training
options.C: Writing formal electronic health record progress notes
options.D: Analyzing statistical trends in community disease outbreaks

explanation: PowerPoint is used to design engaging slide decks for patient education, staff training, and professional presentations. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which practice is recommended when designing slides for patient education to ensure good audience engagement?

options.A: Using small fonts to fit as much clinical text as possible
options.B: Reading every single word straight off the slide screen
options.C: Using large fonts, high contrast, and limiting text per slide
options.D: Avoiding all images and relying solely on complex medical jargon

explanation: Best practices for presentations include using large fonts, high contrast, and limiting text per slide to maintain engagement. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is an important protocol nurses must follow to safeguard patient health information on computer workstations?

options.A: Sharing passwords with trusted colleagues to ensure shift continuity
options.B: Leaving workstations logged in for quick access by anyone
options.C: Adhering to strict password management and logging out when leaving the area
options.D: Printing all digital records and leaving them on public counters

explanation: Safeguarding patient records involves strict password management and logging out of workstations when leaving the area. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is a potential consequence of breaching patient confidentiality through digital software or social media?

options.A: Immediate promotion to an informatics specialist role
options.B: Severe legal consequences and loss of nursing licensure
options.C: Automatic upgrade of hospital software systems
options.D: Mandatory training in advanced spreadsheet analysis

explanation: Breaching patient confidentiality can lead to severe legal penalties and the loss of nursing licensure. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T8#GNS113_U1_T8_h5)
